title: What is known about 1RB1RF_0LC0RF_1RD1LC_---0LE_0RC1LF_1RA0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_0LC0RF_1RD1LC_---0LE_0RC1LF_1RA0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is mostly long blocks of 1s and of 10s. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) finds no halt in the first 1015 steps.

What Lean proves. The whole frame map: 11 tape shapes, 66 cases, each proved for all sizes by a symbolic run (next_sound), and the cases where the map is undefined halt (none_halts). So the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the map, iterated from the frame the run reaches after 6 steps, reaches one of those cases (halts_iff). By native_decide the first 108 frames (about 9.7·1011 machine steps) do not. Whether the orbit ever does is open.

The frame map run far. c/framemap.c iterates the same Lean map in C (its cases generated from the Lean files), jumping over whole sweeps by the Lean lemma sweep. In 62 minutes on one core it went 2.9·1021 frames (1011 rounds, 1.5·1032 machine steps) without reaching a halting case. Seen from the rule form, the map is the tent map on u = 2x/(2x + y), and a halt is the orbit landing exactly on the middle; the closest tapes that could have halted (y odd) were 2 away, such as B(31690290, 63380583).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 4,396 cells have been visited and 2,868 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.339). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.325).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells) runs 1015 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: Halving on the way left, doubling at the left end
claims.text: At consecutive moments the head reaches a new cell, a solid block of p ones at the right end becomes about p/2 copies of 10 at the left end (1171 to 587, 1659 to 831, 691 to 347), and then the alternating block doubles (348 to 698).

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state D was entered 111,425 times, always reading a 1 (D0 halts).

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the machine on a grid
claims.text: For each of the 11 frames and every canonical choice of sizes below 14, the machine reaches exactly the frame, sizes and step count the fitted map predicts (16,632 frames, py/framemap.py verify 14). The map is now proved in Lean; this check is how it was found.

claims.title: The frame map agrees with the run
claims.text: Run from blank tape next to the machine, the fitted map predicts the whole tape at each of the 28,350 frames in the first 5·106 steps (py/framemap.py real 5000000).

claims.title: The whole frame map
claims.text: next in lean/Phases.lean sends each of the 11 frames to the next one the machine reaches, in 66 cases; next_sound proves every case for all parameters, each from a symbolic run in lean/Pieces.lean (generated by py/pieces.py) glued by tape_eq. Where next is undefined (.e l 0 0, .E l 0 0, .f 0 1, .h l 0 1, .i l 0 1, .k l 0, .K l 0) the machine halts (none_halts).

claims.title: Halts if and only if the map reaches an undefined case
claims.text: init_start: the run from blank tape reaches Ph.g 0 1 after 6 steps. halts_iff: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if some iterate of next from there is a frame where next is none.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames
claims.text: no_halt_phases, by native_decide: the first 108 iterates are defined. By the step counts of the fitted map (py/framemap.py run 100000000) that is about 9.7·1011 machine steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.66·10<sup>22</sup> steps (accelerated run, blocks of 2)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/c/rleaccel.cpp (blocks of 2 cells, runs of a block crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths above the minimums it needs; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 1,536,000,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt, in 600 seconds. That is more than 6.66·1022 machine steps. It found no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: Whole sweeps in one statement
claims.text: sweep: for all k, L, J, R, iter (2k) (e L (J+1+k) (R+1+2k)) = some (e (L+2k) (J+1) (R+1)). Nearly every frame of the run is one of the two cases that make up this pair (cases e l (j+2) (r+2) and h l (m+1) (r+2)).

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.9·10<sup>21</sup> frames (1.5·10<sup>32</sup> steps)
claims.text: c/framemap.c iterates next exactly: its 66 cases are generated from lean/Phases.lean and the step counts from lean/Pieces.lean by py/gen_c.py, and whole sweeps are jumped by sweep. It agrees frame by frame with the Python reading of the Lean map for 300,000 frames, and without the jumps it reaches the same frame and step count at 1010 frames. From Ph.g 0 1 it ran 2,916,662,715,542,862,488,166 frames, 1011 of them frames f (one per round of the rule form), to machine step 151,234,372,263,249,191,290,395,350,829,563 (counted exactly in 128 bits), without reaching a case where next is none. Variables reached 2.3·1011.

claims.title: A tent map, and how close the orbit came to the middle
claims.text: With u = 2x/(2x + y), the rules of the rule form are u → 2u (when x < y/2) and u → 2 − 2u (otherwise), up to O(1/(2x + y)), while 2x + y grows by 1 to 4 each round. B(x, 2x + 1), the only halting tape, is the exact middle u ≈ 1/2. Of 10<sup>11</sup> rounds, 33,333,405,819 had y odd (only those can halt); at x ≥ 16 none had d = y − (2x + 1) = 0, and the 16 even values 0 < |d| ≤ 16 had 42 between them (2.6 each). So a d = 0 so far would not have been surprising, nor is its absence (a random model gives about 7% for no hit). The counts near the middle grow by about 0.26 per tenfold growth of x, so a random orbit would still hit eventually, but only after x grows by about 10<sup>4</sup>-fold per expected hit, i.e. the step count by about 10<sup>12</sup>.

claims.title: The rules are a tent map with drift
claims.text: For the rule map of the rule form, in n = 2x + y and d = 2x − y: d ≥ 0 (y even) gives n + 4 and n − 2d + 4; d ≥ 3 (y odd) gives n + 3 and n − 2d + 9; d ≤ −3 gives n + 1 and n + 2d + 7; d = −2 and d = 1 are one-off tapes; the halt is d = −1 and nowhere else. The map is the one of py/rules.py, transcribed; it is checked against the machine there, not in Lean.

claims.title: The binary digits of u predict only about log<sub>2</sub> n rounds
claims.text: The tent orbit of u = 2x/(2x + y), read from its binary digits, agrees with the real fold/double word for floor(log<sub>2</sub> n) − 2 rounds at the median and never more than log<sub>2</sub> n + 6 (1,003 tapes from the first 10<sup>6</sup> rounds, exact rationals). The drift terms take over after that, so the digit reading cannot test the exact middle further than applying the rules.

claims.title: The rules run further
claims.text: 5.07·10<sup>12</sup> rounds of the rule form applied one at a time, with exact step counts: no halt up to machine step 2.0·10<sup>37</sup> (the frame map run reached 1.5·10<sup>32</sup>). Closest tapes with y odd: 2 from the middle (the last, B(144615683250, 289231366503) at step 2.3·10<sup>33</sup>). The 16 even values 0 < |d| ≤ 16 had 55 hits, 3.4 each, d = 0 none (about 3.2% for a random orbit). The near-middle tapes and step counts of the frame map run are reproduced exactly.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape switches between two solid blocks and an alternating-then-solid pair; at the left end the alternating block about doubles at the expense of the solid one.

facts.text: No halt in 2.9·10<sup>21</sup> frames of the Lean frame map, iterated exactly in C (10<sup>11</sup> rounds).
The rounds are the tent map on u = 2x/(2x + y); a halt is landing exactly on the middle. Closest tape with y odd so far: 2 away.
No halt in the run-length accelerator (proved cycle jumps, blocks of 2).
No halt in the first 10<sup>8</sup> frames of the frame map proved in Lean (about 9.7·10<sup>11</sup> machine steps).
It halts if and only if the frame map, iterated from the first frame, reaches a frame where it is undefined.
No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 2 cells).
The alternating block doubles at the expense of the solid block.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 4,396 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell. With a for 10, around step 9.8·107:

• step 98,030,020: 1^1171 a 1^832 B>0 (right end)
  • step 98,032,028: F>0 a^587 1^830 a (left end)
  • step 98,668,985: 1^1659 a 1^347 A>0 (right end)
  • step 98,670,998: F>0 a^831 1^346 a (left end)
  • step 99,190,279: 1^691 a 1^1319 A>0 (right end)
  • step 99,192,296: F>0 a^347 1^1318 a (left end)
  • step 99,440,086: E>0^2 a^698 1^617 a (left end)

At the right end the tape is two solid blocks 1^p 0 1^q; about 2,000 steps later, at the left end, the first block has become an alternating block of about p/2 copies of 10 (1171 to 587, 1659 to 831, 691 to 347). At the left end the alternating block then doubles at the expense of the solid one (348 to 698 while 1316 falls to 617). So this is the doubling of the three machines 1RB1RD_0LC1RA_…_1RF0LD_---0RE again, with an extra quick rewrite between solid and alternating. The width grows like the cube root of the step count.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is D reading a 0. D is entered only from C reading a 0 (1RD), so a halt needs C>0 0. In the first 108 steps D was entered 111,425 times, every time on a 1, and 109,727 of those times at least 7 cells from the left end.
Whether a round can leave C in front of two 0s is open.

sections.heading: The frame map in Lean
html: The frames (blank tape outside; X is the head in state X on the next cell; u^v is v copies of u, so 11^L is 2L ones; a frame counts only at a moment where the head turns round):

• e: 11^L E 00 10^j 1^R
  • E: 1 11^L E 00 10^j 1^R
  • f: 11^L F 1^R
  • F: 1 11^L F 1^R
  • g: F 0 10^j 1^R
  • h: 11^L 0 11^M F 1^R
  • H: 11^L 0 1 11^M F 1^R
  • i: 1 11^L 0 11^M F 1^R
  • I: 1 11^L 0 1 11^M F 1^R
  • k: 11^L 0 1^M B
  • K: 1 11^L 0 1^M B
The map next (Lean names; each variable a natural number):

The map was found by fitting the machine's runs (py/framemap.py) and collapsing the fit into cases (py/pieces.py); Lean then checks every case for all sizes. It is undefined only at .e l 0 0, .E l 0 0, .f 0 1, .h l 0 1, .i l 0 1, .k l 0, .K l 0, and those halt. So the open question is exactly whether the orbit of Ph.g 0 1 reaches one of them; the first 108 frames do not.

sections.heading: Exact tapes, exact step counts
html:
The bbchallenge wiki page of this machine writes its recursion the way the wiki writes Antihydra's: name the tapes exactly, then list the rules. Its top level is one family of tapes (the wiki first defines A(x, y, z) := 1x 0 1y F> 1z and then B(x, y) = A(0, 2x, y)); here each rule also has the exact number of machine steps it takes:

B(x, y) := 0∞ 12x F> 1y 0∞ (x ≥ 1)

This is the same tape as the Lean frame f(x, y) of the section above. A rule goes from B(x, y) to the first moment the tape is its target. In the Lean map, each rule is the run of Lean cases from the frame f(x, y) to the next frame f, except that f(x, 0) is never reached as a frame (the head does not turn round there), so a rule into B(x, 0) and the rule after it show there as one run.

rulefrom → tostepswhen
start0∞ A> 0∞ → B(1, 0)8
swapB(x, 2y) → B(2y + 2, 2x − 2y)4xy − 2y2 + 2x + 16y + 12x ≥ y
swapB(x, 2y + 1) → B(2y + 4, 2x − 2y − 4)4xy − 2y2 + 6x + 12y + 22x > y + 1; for y = 0 it passes B(x − 1, 2)
doubleB(x, 2y) → B(2x + 2, 2y − 2x − 3)2x2 + 10x + 9x < y − 1
doubleB(x, 2y + 1) → B(2x + 2, 2y − 2x − 2)2x2 + 10x + 9x < y
use upB(x, 2x + 2) → B(2x + 1, 0)2x2 + 10x + 7
use upB(x, 2x − 1) → B(2, 4x − 2)2x2 + 14x + 7x ≥ 2; passes B(2x − 1, 0)
haltB(x, 2x + 1) → halt2x2 + 10x + 4D reads 0

The rules and their targets are the wiki's; the step counts are added here. Every B(x, y) with x ≥ 1 falls under exactly one rule, except B(1, 1), which no rule leads to (every target has x ≥ 2); two rules pass another tape of the family on the way, which the wiki, and this table, do not count as a stop.

The rules are not themselves stated in Lean. What is proved is the frame map they are made of: every case of next for all sizes (next_sound in lean/Phases.lean), with the step count of each case in the statement of its piece theorem in lean/Pieces.lean (next_sound itself only says that some number of steps exists), the halts (none_halts; the halt row ends in the case .h l 0 1) and halts_iff. python3 py/rules.py checks each row three ways: direct simulation from 2,449 tapes B(x, y) (x, y < 50) to the rule's target or the halt, with the step count of the table and no other tape of the family on the way except the one named; the Lean cases from f(x, y) to the next frame f, giving the same; and the run from blank tape, where the 388 visits of the first 107 steps are exactly the rules' orbit from B(1, 0) with the same step counts, and the frames f of the Lean map are the visits with y > 0. The Lean map followed for 5·105 frames (3.4·108 steps, 1,273 frames f) agrees with the rules too. So if the rules hold for all sizes, as they do on every tape checked, the machine halts iff they lead from B(1, 0) to some B(x, 2x + 1).

For example B(1, 16) = 12 F> 116: B(4, 11) after 21 steps, B(10, 0) after 81, B(2, 20) after 32, B(6, 13) after 37, and the halt 136 steps later: 307 steps in all, which is what direct simulation gives.

sections.heading: A tent map, and the middle it has not hit
html: The rule form below has one family of tapes B(x, y). Put u = 2x/(2x + y), the share of the tape left of the head. Up to a correction of order 1/(2x + y), a round doubles u when it is below 1/2 (the swap with x < y/2) and sends it to 2 − 2u when it is above (the swap with x ≥ y/2): the tent map, the textbook chaotic map that reads off the binary digits of u. Meanwhile the total 2x + y grows by 1 to 4 per round, which feeds new digits in. The only halting tape is B(x, 2x + 1), where u sits exactly on the middle, so the question is whether a chaotic orbit on a slowly growing grid ever lands exactly on its centre.

c/framemap.c runs the Lean map itself: its 66 cases and their step counts are generated from the Lean files, and long sweeps (two cases repeated, e L J R → e (L+2) (J−1) (R−2)) are jumped in one go by the Lean lemma sweep. In 62 minutes on one core: 2.9·1021 frames, 1011 rounds, 1.5·1032 machine steps, no halt. With d = y − (2x + 1) the distance from the middle, the record approaches were:

round tapedmachine step
B(1014, 2030)17.98·108
B(278826, 557655)21.65·1016
B(5118454, 10236910)11.02·1020
B(31690290, 63380583)22.43·1022
B(2599201108, 5198402216)−11.34·1028
B(47350001284, 94700002570)18.09·1031

Only tapes with y odd can halt (d then is even), and those come only from the swap with x < y/2. Of the 1011 rounds a third had y odd. At x ≥ 16 none had d = 0, while the 16 even values 0 < |d| ≤ 16 were hit 42 times together, 2.6 each. So the miss is not yet evidence of anything: a random orbit would have missed with probability about 7%. Hits near the middle accrue at about 0.26 per tenfold growth of x, which is why a random model says it halts eventually but cannot say when: about one expected hit per 104-fold growth of x, or 1012-fold of the step count. Nothing here proves either answer; a proof would need an arithmetic reason that keeps the exact middle out of reach.

sections.heading: Reading the rounds off the binary digits of u
sections.html:
The tent map has a famous shortcut: its whole orbit can be read off the binary digits of the starting point. Write u = 0.b1b2b3… in binary; then the k-th step of the tent map doubles when bk = bk−1 and folds when they differ (b0 = 0), because doubling is a shift of the digits and folding is a shift that flips them. If the rounds of this machine were exactly the tent map, the digits of one tape’s u would tell us its next rounds without running them, and perhaps say something about landing on the middle far beyond the 1032 steps run so far.

They are not exactly the tent map, and the correction is known exactly. In the coordinates n = 2x + y and d = 2x − y every rule is

whennew nnew d
d ≥ 0, y even (fold)n + 4n − 2d + 4
d ≥ 3, y odd (fold)n + 3n − 2d + 9
d ≤ −3 (double)n + 1n + 2d + 7

plus two one-off tapes (d = −2 and d = 1) and the halt at d = −1, nowhere else (Lean, lean/Tent.lean, checked by the kernel). So d/n = 2u − 1 goes to 1 − 2|d/n| plus a small term c/n, and every later round doubles that small term. After about log2 n rounds it has grown to the size of u itself and the digits of the old u no longer say anything. Try it on the real run:

Over 1,003 tapes sampled from the first million rounds, the digit reading agreed with the real rounds for floor(log2 n) − 2 rounds at the median, never more than 6 rounds past log2 n (py/tent.py). The histogram below is the same count, recomputed in your browser over the first 300,000 rounds.

So the digits are a dead end for the halting question: at n around 1011 a tape’s digits predict about 35 rounds, and beyond that the only way to know the rounds is to apply them. That is cheap, though: c/rounds.c applies the rules one at a time with exact 256-bit step counts, 4.7 times faster per round than the frame map run above. Run to 8·1011 rounds: 7.7·1034 machine steps, 500 times further than the frame map run, and no halt. Two new tapes came within 2 of the middle, B(12459332366, 24918664731) and B(144615683250, 289231366503). The 16 even values 0 < |d| ≤ 16 next to the middle were hit 50 times together, 3.1 each, and d = 0 never; a random orbit misses with probability about 4.5%. Resumed from there to 5.07·1012 rounds: 2.0·1037 machine steps, 250 times further again, no halt and no new tape within 2 of the middle; the 16 even neighbours of the middle have 55 hits, 3.4 each, and d = 0 still none (about 3.2% for a random orbit). Still no evidence either way.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.339). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.325).
After 109 steps the tape spans 4,396 cells (2,260 left of the start, 1,268 right), with a density of 1s of 0.652.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: doubling between an alternating and a solid block
summary: Its tape switches between two solid blocks and an alternating-then-solid pair; at the left end the alternating block about doubles at the expense of the solid one. Accelerated run: no halt in 6.66e22 steps.
